questions.question_text: In interpersonal psychotherapy, clinical depression is conceptualized with which of the following THREE components?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal psychotherapy was originally conceptualized as intervening in symptom formation and social functioning; it influences personality less because of its short duration.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the principal metabolite of dopamine?
When is sexual preference established typically?
questions.explanation: Gender identity is established by age 3. Sexual preference, however, is typically established during middle childhood.

questions.question_text: Which of the following treatment programs has significant empirical support for adolescents with depression?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal therapy has received empirical support of efficacy for depressed adolescents.

questions.question_text: True or False: In preschool children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), the inattentive subtype is more common.
questions.explanation: The hyperactive subtype is more common; however, the symptoms related to hyperactivity tend to decrease with age.

questions.question_text: What proportion of children in sub-Saharan Africa are infected with HIV?
questions.explanation: Approximately one-fourth of the young population in sub-Saharan Africa is infected.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Adolescents with sleep problems are less likely to develop learning difficulties or have impaired academic performance
The mean length of sleep for high school students is approximately 12.3 hours a night
Adolescents experience an increase in appetite, referred to as developmental hyperphagia, which is seen across species
The sleep phase shift seen in adolescence occurs due to earlier night-onset and earlier morning-termination of melatonin secretion

correct_answer.text: Adolescents experience an increase in appetite, referred to as developmental hyperphagia, which is seen across species

correct_answers.text: Adolescents experience an increase in appetite, referred to as developmental hyperphagia, which is seen across species

questions.question_text: What is the range suggested by epidemiological studies for the percentage of children with diagnosable psychiatric disorders?
questions.explanation: Up to 9% suffer from 'extreme functional impairments' from psychiatric disorders.

questions.question_text: In assessing a child who presents with somatic symptoms it is important to:

options.text: Refrain from asking about prior treatment experiences, which have likely been alienating or discouraging
See the child before the parents
Explore timing, context, and social reinforcement of any symptoms
Enlist the patient's view by making a statement such as 'nothing is wrong, so what do you think is wrong?'
Try to convey over time how the symptoms are purely psychological

correct_answer.text: Explore timing, context, and social reinforcement of any symptoms

correct_answers.text: Explore timing, context, and social reinforcement of any symptoms

questions.explanation: Remember also, many patients—or anyone, for that matter—know a friend or relative who was reassured about a symptom and later found to have serious physical disease.

questions.question_text: True or False: More than 50% of children who experiment with drugs go on to become regular users.

options.text: Children and parents are more accurate reporters of the child's externalizing symptoms and other adults are better reporters of internalizing symptoms
Children are more accurate reporters of their externalizing symptoms and parents more accurate reporters of their child's internalizing symptoms
Children are more accurate reporters of their internalizing symptoms and parents more accurate reporters of their child's externalizing symptoms
Children and parents are more accurate reporters of the child's internalizing symptoms and other adults are better reporters of externalizing symptoms

questions.question_text: In the multisite study, Treatment of ADHD in Children with Tourette's syndrome (TACT), 136 children (ages 7–14) with ADHD and a chronic tic disorder were randomized to one of four treatments: clonidine, methylphenidate, clonidine and methylphenidate, or placebo. All three active treatments were superior to placebo on teacher and parent measures of ADHD

Combined treatment with clonidine and methylphenidate was superior to placebo on teacher and parent measures of ADHD

questions.question_text: True or False: There is a higher rate of psychosis among patients with epilepsy.
questions.explanation: The sum of the data suggests this is true and seems to be associated most strongly with temporal lobe epilepsy.

questions.question_text: ALL of the following are reasons why scores among tests assessing psychological functioning may vary EXCEPT:

options.text: The tests may not be correlated or only moderately related
Scores may improve because of familiarity with the test or test items or prior exposure

correct_answers.text: The tests may have the same content despite differing in their name

questions.question_text: Speece and Brent concluded that most studies found the age of acquisition of the three concepts of death they reviewed—irreversibility, nonfunctionality, and universality—to occur between:
questions.explanation: Most children acquire the concepts of death between ages 5 and 7.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum acceptable level of reliability for a neuropsychological or psychological test?
questions.explanation: Reliability is represented by the reliability coefficient, symbolized by the letter r with two identical subscripts and range from 0.00 (no association between scores) to 1.00 (perfect reliability).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of acute otitis media and its sequelae?

correct_answers.text: It is very uncommon after age 6 years

questions.explanation: Acute otitis media (AOM) affects about two-thirds of the children in the age range of 6 to 24 months.
